registry_polymers_and_waxes.latent_heat: none: atactic polystyrene is amorphous, no melting endotherm
none: 161 J/g 100 % reference (Wunderlich via TN048) but no sourced grade crystallinity

refused_by_policy.reason: poly(vinyl chloride) is nearly amorphous and dehydrochlorinates on heating instead of melting cleanly; no sourced crystallinity of a rigid grade was found (its 176 J/g 100 % reference, B. Wunderlich, Thermal Analysis, Academic Press 1990, pp. 417-431 as quoted by R. L. Blaine, TA Instruments TN048, would have nothing to multiply)

virgin PTFE powder melts first far more crystalline than the sintered polymer (about twofold); only sintered PTFE has an open crystallinity measurement (39.5-43.1 % against 82 J/g, doi:10.3390/polym17101380)

poly(lactic acid) crystallinity runs from about 0 to 26 % with moulding and annealing history (Ingeo-type PLA plaques 19-25.7 %, doi:10.1021/acsomega.6c03726; a PLA/PCL blend 0.4 %, Europe PMC PMC12473204), so no grade value can be chosen without the history
